chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami and Zayd al-Shahham, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered us to say the Talbiyah and not specify anything, and he said, 'The Talbiyah with pronouns (implicit subject) is more beloved to me.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْإِضْمَارِ: Those with implicit pronouns (referring to the grammatical structure of the Talbiyah where the subject 'we' is implied in the verb)
key_terms.نُسَمِّيَ: To specify or mention a particular detail/intention
key_terms.نُلَبِّيَ: To recite the Talbiyah (the declaration of readiness to meet God during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for reciting the Talbiyah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi highlights the Prophetic preference for the concise, implicit form of the Talbiyah ('Labbayk') over explicit declarations of specific intent, reflecting the Shia emphasis on following the Imam's preferred mode of worship. It underscores the principle that while general invocation is sufficient, adhering to the specific stylistic preferences of the Ahl al-Bayt enhances the spiritual quality of the ritual. This guidance serves to unify the Ummah under the Imam's teachings while allowing flexibility in the expression of devotion.
